claims: Mortgage brokers earn a commission typically 1–2% of the loan amount.
Mortgage brokers' commissions are usually paid by the lender at closing.
Mortgage brokers' commissions are usually not paid by the borrower.
In most cases, the lender pays the broker a fee often 1% to 2% of the total loan amount after the loan closes.
In some cases, a borrower may pay a broker fee directly.
The cost paid by the lender to the broker can sometimes be built into the interest rate or closing costs.
Mortgage brokers must complete pre-licensing mandated training.
Mortgage brokers must pass the National Mortgage License System (NMLS) test.
Mortgage brokers must maintain licensing through ongoing education.
